lessons.title: Big O Notation
lessons.concept: Big O describes the upper bound of running time (worst case) as input size grows. Common: O(1), O(log n), O(n), O(n log n), O(n²).
lessons.worked_example: Single loop over n → O(n). Nested loop → O(n²). Binary search → O(log n).
mistakes: Confusing Big O with exact time

lessons.title: Complexity Reference
lessons.concept: Array: access O(1), search O(n). BST: search O(log n) avg. Hash: O(1) avg. Merge sort O(n log n). Quick sort worst O(n²).
lessons.worked_example: Hash table avg O(1), worst O(n). Binary search requires sorted array.
mistakes: Assuming BST always O(log n) (degenerate → O(n))
Assuming quick sort always O(n log n)

practice.question: What does Big O describe?
practice.explanation: Big O = upper bound of running time (worst case).

practice.question: Hash table average time complexity?
practice.explanation: Hash table average O(1); worst O(n) with collisions.

questions.question: Merge sort worst-case?
questions.explanation: Merge sort always O(n log n), stable, needs extra space.

questions.question: Quick sort worst case?
questions.explanation: Quick sort worst O(n²) (e.g., sorted input with bad pivot).

questions.question: Binary search requirement?
questions.explanation: Binary search requires a sorted array.
